precedent.topic: Whether valid progress photo updates always persist and audit, or can be rolled back as replays, and how replay is identified
quotes: update_progress_photo: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST validate optional section project scope, change only caption/section/client_visible/updated_at/updated_by, and append AuditAction.PHOTO_UPDATE atomically without changing file_ref, progress, or finance.

update_progress_photo: [DEPENDENCY_BOUNDARY] MUST open exactly one transaction, read the photo only through tx.progress_photos().get_progress_photo with photo_id, resolve a supplied section only through tx.project_sections().get_project_section with context.project_id inside that same transaction, write only through tx.progress_photos().update_progress_photo, append the audit only through tx.audit(), and on success commit exactly once (a replay or a validation failure closes it by rollback instead); it MUST NOT call validate_project_section, open a second transaction while its own is active, or use a legacy transaction-level photo or project-section method.

update_progress_photo: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] MUST append exactly one AuditAction.PHOTO_UPDATE success audit through tx.audit() with entity_kind PROGRESS_PHOTO, entity_id equal to the canonical string of the updated photo_id, and reason_code None; a non-null reason_code on a success audit is rejected by the audit writer and MUST NOT be supplied.
precedent.why: The update requirements mention a replay rollback path but neither define how an update becomes a replay nor reconcile that path with the unconditional write-and-audit obligations.

topics.topic: Handling newlines in canonical_path to preserve one-line log records
questions: If canonical_path contains a newline, must it be escaped or altered to keep the record to one line, or must it be written whole?

quotes: MUST build one line of exactly four labelled fields in this order and shape, so an operator log parser does not change between builds: 'rid=<request id> method=<method> path=<canonical path without query string> status=<status>'.

The line is bounded in its fields, not in its length: the path field is the canonical_path argument, which the caller already took from _canonical_path over the request path without its query string, written whole; it MUST NOT be truncated or shortened.
judgement.why: A canonical path containing a newline cannot both be written whole as the path argument and produce a one-line record unless the text specifies an escaping or normalization rule.

topics.topic: Redaction of credential or identity material in canonical paths
questions: If the canonical path itself contains credential or identity material, must the path be redacted, or must it be written whole without truncation or shortening?

quotes: The line is bounded in its fields, not in its length: the path field is the canonical_path argument, which the caller already took from _canonical_path over the request path without its query string, written whole; it MUST NOT be truncated or shortened.
Headers, cookies, query values, bodies, credentials, identities, raw exception text and configuration values MUST NOT appear in it.
judgement.why: Writing the canonical path whole conflicts with the prohibition on credentials and identities appearing in the record when that path contains such material.
